title: fix(plugin-dashboard,i18n): translate the dashboard config sidebar (#4748)
body:
Fixes #4748

`WidgetConfigPanel` and `DashboardConfigPanel` build the dashboard config sidebar's `ConfigPanelSchema` — breadcrumb, section titles, field labels, placeholders, help sentences and option labels — and neither imported a translation hook at all. All 61 user-visible strings were English literals. Both are exported from the package barrel and mounted by `DashboardWithConfig`, so the panel a user opens to configure a dashboard or a widget stayed English inside a console that had translated around it.

Verified at head `0f9d59527`.

## What landed

A new `dashboard.config.*` namespace — **75 keys, all ten packs** — and both panels routed through `useConfigPanelTranslation`, a `createSafeTranslation` hook whose `CONFIG_PANEL_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS` map keeps provider-less hosts on English.

**Namespace by measurement, not preference.** `MetricWidget` already reads `dashboard.trend.*` and `DashboardFilterBar` reads `dashboard.filters.*`, both through `createSafeTranslation`. A third area of the same namespace is the shape those two establish; the hook module mirrors `plugin-detail`'s `useDetailTranslation.ts` / `fields`' `useFieldTranslation.ts`.

**Fresh keys, not the retired block.** The packs carried a top-level `configPanel.*` namespace of 16 keys whose vocabulary reads like this panel's. It had zero readers and was deleted by #4747. Keys here are authored against the wording the panels actually ship — that block was never validated against a shipped label and covers 16 of the 61 strings. Where the two name the same word the *translations* are reused, so the packs stay internally consistent.

**Keys are literal arguments of `t()`, never rows of a `{ value, key }` table.** The option groups (11 widget types, 8 colours, 7 refresh intervals, 3 themes, 4 breadcrumb tails) were written as lookup tables first. Measured: that shape put all 33 of those keys on the dead-key report as NEEDS-REVIEW and made `check-i18n-call-site-keys` skip them as dynamic-key sites — 33 keys that neither i18n gate could see. Rewritten as builder functions returning literal `t('…')` calls, both gates cover all 75.

## English is byte-identical, asserted positively

`createSafeTranslation` serves the defaults map with no provider and the `en` pack with one, so a row that drifts from either renders two labels for one control (the #4401 class). Every row is compared **in both directions** against `ORIGINAL_LITERALS`, a frozen hand-transcribed table of the pre-change English, at codepoint level so `…` cannot pass for `...`.

Three test files, split by what each can see:

| file | what it owns |
|---|---|
| `ConfigPanel.i18nWiring.test.tsx` | builds both schemas with an identity `t`, so every translated string equals its own key. Leg 1: every user-visible string in the built schema **is** a key — a surviving English literal is not a key and fails by naming itself. Leg 2: the full expected key layout, so a swapped key fails too. Leg 3: 75 rows × map + pack vs the frozen table. |
| `ConfigPanel.noProviderLabels.test.tsx` | mounts **no** provider — the English fallback reaching the real DOM, including what the schema walk cannot see: the dataset combobox, member chips, add control and empty states produced inside `custom` fields' `render()`. |
| `ConfigPanel.localeLabels.test.tsx` | zh (non-Latin) + de (Latin) through `I18nProvider`. |

The provider-less file is deliberately its own file: `createI18n` registers its instance as react-i18next's module-global default and the registration survives `cleanup()`, so a no-provider assertion sharing a file with a provider mount silently resolves against the last language used.

## Reverse verification

Directions written before running.

**Ablation A** — both panels reverted to `origin/main`'s hardcoded English, packs and tests kept:
- `ConfigPanel.localeLabels.test.tsx` → **RED**, 5/5, with the defect's own signature: `expected [ 'Dashboard', 'Chart' ] to deeply equal [ '仪表盘', '图表' ]`, and the same for `[ 'Dashboard', 'Diagramm' ]`. That file *is* the bug.
- `ConfigPanel.noProviderLabels.test.tsx` → **GREEN**, 9/9. Predicted green: it pins the English fallback, which this change deliberately does not move. Red there would have meant the English bytes shifted.

**Ablation B** — one row (`dashboard.config.field.columns`) deleted from the defaults map: red on all three legs at once — `notKeys` = `['dashboard.config.field.columns']`, key-set 75 vs 74, the row comparison, `Unable to find an element with the text: Columns`, and the raw-key guard catching `dashboard.config.field.columns` in the DOM.

Both restored with `git checkout` against the committed branch — the fix was committed before either ablation, so a real restore point existed. No `git stash` at any point.

## Gates, all at `0f9d59527`

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-dashboard/ packages/i18n/` | 106 files, **1368 passed** |
| `check:i18n-keys` | green — 2549 pack-backed sites, 2495/2495 literal keys resolve, interpolation parity clean |
| `check:i18n-drift` | **75 added, 0 changed** |
| `check:i18n-dead-keys` | `dashboard.config` appears **0 times** in the report — the namespace has readers |
| `all-locales-key-parity`, `ellipsis-glyph-3878`, `untranslated-identity-4376`, `de-quote-pairing-3876` | green (in the i18n suite above) |
| `type-check` (both packages) | green |
| `lint` (both packages) | 0 errors |
| `check-changeset-presence` / `-fixed` / `-no-major` | green — `plugin-dashboard` + `i18n` patch |
| `check-control-bytes` + `grep -naP` self-scan | clean |
| `check:phantom-deps`, `lint:coverage`, `type-check:coverage` | green |

Gate set re-derived against the actual changed paths from the CI workflows rather than taken from the dispatch list alone; `check:phantom-deps`, `lint:coverage` and `type-check:coverage` are the additions that found.

## Notes for review

- **One correction mid-implementation, worth flagging:** an early grep over `config-panel-renderer.tsx` alone suggested `ConfigField.helpText` was declared-but-never-rendered, and I nearly filed that as a finding. It is rendered — by `config-field-renderer.tsx`, which wraps every control type (custom ones included) in a paragraph carrying it. So the four help sentences are genuinely user-visible, they are the longest copy the panel serves, and they now have their own DOM coverage in both English and zh.
- `buildWidgetSchema` / `buildDashboardSchema` are exported from their modules (not the barrel) so the wiring can be asserted exhaustively. This follows the file's own precedent — `sanitizeDraftForType` is exported the same way for the same reason — and costs one more `react-refresh/only-export-components` **warning** on a file that already had two.
- **Overlap with #4747, measured after it landed.** This branch was cut from `616a2a547`, before #4747 deleted `configPanel.*` and `renderer.*` from the same ten pack files; #4747 has since merged as `f34226ea9`. The overlap is clean, by construction rather than luck: there is no key overlap (these are fresh keys under `dashboard.config.*`), and the new block was deliberately inserted inside the `dashboard` namespace immediately before `trend:` — roughly 30 lines from the top-level `configPanel:` block #4747 removed — so the two land as separate hunks. `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` at `138ab04d5` reports the ten pack files changed on both sides and **zero conflict markers**.
- Filed out of scope: **#4750** — `ConfigPanelRenderer`'s own footer defaults `saveLabel = 'Save'` / `discardLabel = 'Discard'` in `@object-ui/components`, which no caller overrides, so every config panel's footer (report, dashboard, widget) stays English. It belongs in the renderer, not per-caller, or the dashboard's footer would translate while `ReportConfigPanel`'s stayed English.
- `#4746`, `#4730`, `#4024` and `#1713` are referenced above for context and are not addressed here.
